drivingQuestion: Why need border marks on a jointly built partition?
outcomeNote: Rav Ashi: the ruling covers a party who marked first

segments.he: אֲבָל אִם עָשׂוּ מִדַּעַת שְׁנֵיהֶם. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: לָא יַעֲשׂוּ לֹא זֶה וְלֹא זֶה! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא צְרִיכָא, דִּקְדֵים חַד מִנַּיְיהוּ וַעֲבַד דִּידֵיהּ, וְאִי לָא עָבֵיד חַבְרֵיהּ – אָמַר: דִּידֵיהּ הוּא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: Nevertheless, in a place where it is not customary to build a partition between two people’s fields, «if they made» such a partition «with the agreement of the two of them,» they build it in the middle, i.e., on the property line, and make a border mark on the one side and on the other side. Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that the space where the wall stood and the stones belong to both of them, to be divided equally. «Rava from Parzika said to Rav Ashi: Neither this one nor that one should make» a border mark. Rav Ashi «said to him: No,» this ruling «is necessary» in a case «where one of them went ahead and made» a border mark «for himself,» so that «if his neighbor does not make» one as well, the first one «will say» that «it is» entirely «his.»

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא מפרזיקא לרב אשי
moves.about: a jointly built partition needs no border mark on either side
needed where one party already made his own mark
